name: The New Saints FC
content:
The New Saints Football Club (commonly known as TNS) is a professional football club that represents both Oswestry in England and Llansantffraid-ym-Mechain in Wales. The club was originally formed in 1959 as Llansantffraid FC and later merged with Oswestry Town, eventually developing into its modern identity. Despite being based in England, the team competes in the Welsh football league system and plays its home matches at Park Hall in Oswestry.

Over time, The New Saints have become the most successful club in Welsh domestic football. They have won numerous Cymru Premier titles and regularly dominate the league, often finishing at or near the top of the table. The club has also achieved multiple victories in domestic cup competitions, including the Welsh Cup and Welsh League Cup, establishing a strong record of consistent success over several decades.

TNS have also represented Wales in European competitions such as the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League, and UEFA Europa Conference League. In recent years, they made history by becoming the first club from the Welsh domestic system to reach the group or league phase of a major UEFA competition. This achievement further strengthened their reputation as the leading force in Welsh club football.

name: Barry Town United FC
content:
Barry Town United FC is a Welsh football club based in Barry, Vale of Glamorgan. The club was originally formed in 1912 as Barry AFC and has since developed into one of the most historically significant teams in Welsh domestic football. They play their home matches at Jenner Park, a long-established stadium in the town, and are commonly known for their yellow and blue colours.

Throughout its history, Barry Town United has experienced periods of major success, particularly during the late 20th century. The club became one of the dominant forces in Welsh football, winning multiple domestic league titles and Welsh Cups, and regularly competing in European competitions as a representative of Wales. They have also played in various English leagues in earlier stages of their development before fully integrating into the Welsh football system.

In more recent years, the club has been recognised for its supporter-led structure and recovery after financial difficulties. Barry Town United returned to competitive stability within the Welsh football pyramid and continues to compete in the Cymru Premier, the top tier of Welsh football. The club remains known for its strong community identity and its role in developing Welsh domestic football.

name: Bangor City FC
content:
Bangor City FC was a Welsh football club based in Bangor, Gwynedd, founded in 1876. It was one of the oldest clubs in Wales and became an important part of the country’s early football development. The team was traditionally known as “The Citizens” and played their home matches at Farrar Road for much of their history before later moving to Nantporth. Throughout its existence, the club competed in various Welsh, English, and cross-border competitions before the creation of a unified Welsh league system in 1992.

During its history, Bangor City achieved significant domestic success, including multiple Welsh Cup victories and appearances in European competitions. One of their most notable achievements came in the early 1960s when they won the Welsh Cup and competed in the European Cup Winners’ Cup against strong continental opposition such as Napoli. The club remained a regular participant in European tournaments in later decades, particularly after becoming part of the League of Wales (now Cymru Premier), where they also won league titles.

In the modern era, Bangor City experienced both sporting success and serious financial and administrative difficulties. Despite winning major domestic honours and remaining competitive for periods, the club suffered from instability, licensing issues, and relegations. These problems ultimately led to their withdrawal from competition and dissolution in 2025, ending a long and historic chapter in Welsh football.

name: Connah's Quay Nomads FC
content:
Connah’s Quay Nomads FC is a Welsh professional football club based in Connah’s Quay, Flintshire. The club was formed in the post-war period and has grown into one of the leading teams in the Cymru Premier, the top division of Welsh football. They play their home matches at Deeside Stadium and are commonly known simply as “The Nomads.” Over time, the club has established itself as a consistent competitor at the highest level of the Welsh football pyramid.

The Nomads achieved their breakthrough success in the late 2010s and early 2020s, becoming one of the strongest sides in domestic competition. They have won the Cymru Premier title and also secured multiple domestic cup victories, including the Welsh Cup. One of their most notable achievements came in the 2019–20 season when they won the league for the first time in their history, marking a major milestone for the club. They have also regularly competed in European tournaments such as the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa Conference League, gaining experience against international opposition.

In addition to domestic success, Connah’s Quay Nomads have been involved in several memorable European and cup campaigns. They have recorded notable wins in qualifying rounds and reached advanced stages of domestic cup competitions, often challenging more established clubs. Despite some periods of managerial changes and squad rebuilding, the club has maintained its position as a top-tier Welsh team and continues to compete near the top of the Cymru Premier standings.

name: Rhyl FC
content:
Rhyl FC was a Welsh football club based in the seaside town of Rhyl, Denbighshire, and was originally founded in the late 19th century. The club became known as the “Lilywhites” and played its home matches at Belle Vue, a ground that served as its base for more than a century. Rhyl developed through various early regional leagues before becoming part of the structured Welsh football system, eventually establishing itself as one of the notable clubs in North Wales.

Throughout its history, Rhyl enjoyed periods of significant success in Welsh domestic football. The club won multiple Welsh Premier League titles and several Welsh Cups, particularly during the 2000s when it was one of the strongest teams in the country. It also regularly competed in European competitions, representing Wales in UEFA tournaments, and achieved notable league campaigns in both the Welsh top division and lower tiers after relegations and promotions.

In its later years, Rhyl faced financial difficulties and instability, which led to administrative problems and eventual withdrawal from competition. The club was formally wound up in 2021 after ceasing football operations in 2020, ending more than a century of history. Following its collapse, a phoenix club was created in Rhyl to continue football in the town and preserve its footballing identity.

name: Llanelli Town AFC
content:
Llanelli Town AFC is a Welsh football club based in Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, originally founded in 1896. The club developed through early Welsh and English non-league systems and established Stebonheath Park as its home ground in the early 20th century. In its early years, Llanelli became one of the stronger semi-professional sides in Wales, regularly competing in regional leagues and the Welsh Cup, and building a reputation as a competitive club outside the top professional tiers.

During the 20th century, Llanelli Town made several unsuccessful attempts to join the English Football League, coming close on multiple occasions but never being elected. After the formation of the League of Wales in 1992, the club became one of its founding members. Over the following decades, Llanelli experienced a mix of promotions and relegations between the top tier and lower divisions, but also achieved notable success, including winning the Welsh Premier League and domestic cup competitions during the late 2000s and early 2010s.

In 2013, the original club was wound up due to financial problems, but it was quickly reformed as a phoenix club, allowing football in Llanelli to continue. The new version of the club restarted in the lower tiers of the Welsh football pyramid and worked its way back up through promotions, eventually returning to higher divisions. Today, Llanelli Town continues to compete within the Welsh league system and remains an important club with a strong local identity and history.

name: Cwmbrân Town AFC
content:
Cwmbrân Town AFC is a Welsh football club based in Cwmbrân, Torfaen, founded in 1951 following the disbanding of Whiteheads AFC. The club began competing in junior leagues before joining the Welsh Football League in 1960. In 1975 they moved to Cwmbrân Stadium, which became their long-term home. The club experienced early instability, including relegation from the top division in 1978, but quickly returned to the higher level in the early 1980s.

The club became one of the founding members of the League of Wales in 1992 and achieved immediate success by winning the inaugural league title in the 1992–93 season. This victory marked the peak of their domestic achievements and qualified them for European competition for the first time, where they faced Cork City in the UEFA Champions League qualifiers. In the following years, Cwmbrân remained competitive at the top level and also reached multiple Welsh Cup finals, which allowed further appearances in European tournaments.

From the late 1990s and especially the 2000s, the club experienced a decline due to financial difficulties and poor results, leading to relegation from the top tier in 2007. They dropped further down the Welsh football pyramid in subsequent years, facing multiple relegations and rebuilding phases. Despite these struggles, the club has continued to exist and compete at lower levels, maintaining its identity within Welsh football history as a former league champion and European participant.

name: Inter Cardiff FC
content:
Inter Cardiff FC was a Welsh football club based in Cardiff, formed in 1990 through the merger of A.FC Cardiff and Sully FC The club competed in the Welsh football system and quickly became part of the League of Wales (now Cymru Premier). It initially established itself as a competitive side in top-flight Welsh football and was based in the Cardiff area throughout its existence. The club also went through a brief name change to Inter CableTel in the mid-1990s before reverting back to Inter Cardiff.

During the 1990s, Inter Cardiff enjoyed a strong period in domestic competition, regularly finishing near the top of the Welsh league. The club was particularly successful in cup competitions, winning the Welsh Senior Cup in 1999 and the Welsh Football League Cup in 1997. They also consistently competed in European tournaments, representing Wales in the UEFA Cup on several occasions, although they were eliminated in the early qualifying rounds against stronger opposition.

In 2000, Inter Cardiff merged with UWIC (University of Wales Institute, Cardiff) to form a new club, which later became known as Cardiff Metropolitan University FC This merger effectively ended Inter Cardiff as a separate entity, but its legacy continued through the successor club, which remains active in the Welsh football system today. The club is remembered for its strong 1990s performances and its role in the early years of the national league.

name: Bala Town FC
content:
Bala Town FC is a Welsh football club based in Bala, Gwynedd, founded in 1880. The club is known as “The Lakesiders” and plays its home matches at Maes Tegid. Over its long history, Bala Town developed through regional leagues in North Wales before gradually progressing through the Welsh football pyramid, eventually reaching the national level and establishing itself in the Cymru Premier, the top tier of Welsh football.

The club spent many decades in lower and regional competitions before achieving significant progress in the 2000s. After gaining promotion through the Welsh league system, Bala Town reached the Cymru Premier and began competing regularly against the strongest teams in Wales. This period marked a major step forward in the club’s development, as it became a stable top-flight side and started to challenge for higher league positions and cup competitions.

In the modern era, Bala Town has become a competitive and consistent team in Welsh football, often finishing in the upper half of the Cymru Premier table. The club has also achieved success in domestic cups, including winning the Welsh Cup, and has represented Wales in European competitions such as UEFA qualifying tournaments. Bala Town is now recognised as one of the established clubs in the Welsh domestic system with a strong semi-professional structure and growing reputation.

name: Airbus UK Broughton FC
content:
Airbus UK Broughton FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Broughton, Flintshire. The club was formed in 1946 as a works team for the Airbus aircraft factory, where aircraft wings are manufactured, and it is nicknamed “The Wingmakers.” Over the years, the team has developed through local and regional leagues before becoming part of the Welsh football pyramid, eventually reaching the national level. It plays its home matches at the Hollingsworth Group Stadium, which is located next to the Airbus factory site and is known for its distinctive setting near an active runway.

The club steadily progressed through the Welsh football system, winning lower-division titles before earning promotion to higher tiers. A major milestone came in the early 2000s when Airbus UK Broughton reached the Cymru Premier for the first time after winning the Cymru Alliance. This marked their arrival in the top flight of Welsh football, where they competed against the strongest clubs in the country. During this period, the club experienced both challenges and achievements, including avoiding relegation battles and improving its overall competitiveness.

In the 2010s, Airbus UK Broughton had one of its strongest spells, finishing high enough in the league to qualify for European competitions on several occasions. The club competed in UEFA Europa League qualifying rounds, gaining experience against international opponents, and also reached the Welsh Cup final in 2016. However, after a difficult 2016–17 season, they were relegated from the Cymru Premier. Since then, the club has continued to compete in the Welsh football pyramid, moving between divisions but remaining an established semi-professional side.

name: Newtown AFC
content:
Newtown AFC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Newtown, Powys. The club was founded in 1875 and is one of the oldest football clubs in Wales, as well as one of the founding members of the Football Association of Wales. It plays its home matches at Latham Park and competes in the Cymru Premier, the top tier of Welsh football. Over its long history, the club has become a key representative of mid-Wales football.

The club’s early history is complex, originating from several local sides such as Newtown and White Stars, which were active in the 1870s. These teams were involved in the earliest editions of the Welsh Cup, with White Stars winning the competition in 1878–79. After several mergers and reorganisations, the modern version of Newtown AFC was established in the 1880s. The club went on to win the Welsh Cup in 1894–95 and remained an important part of Welsh football development throughout the 20th century.

In the modern era, Newtown has been a consistent member of the Welsh top flight since the formation of the League of Wales in 1992. The club has finished as league runners-up twice in the 1990s and has also competed in UEFA competitions against European opposition. While not among the dominant clubs, Newtown has maintained stability in the Cymru Premier for decades and is known for its strong community identity and long-standing presence in Welsh football.

name: Penybont FC
content:
Penybont FC is a Welsh football club based in Bridgend, South Wales. The club was formed in 2013 following the merger of Bridgend Town and Bryntirion Athletic, bringing together two established local sides to create a single progressive team. Penybont plays its home matches at the DragonBet Stadium (formerly Bryntirion Park) and competes in the Cymru Premier, the top tier of Welsh football.

After its formation, the club quickly established itself as a strong competitor in the Welsh Football League system, achieving promotion to higher divisions and continuing to develop both on and off the pitch. In 2018–19, Penybont won the Welsh Football League Division One, securing promotion to the Cymru Premier for the first time in the club’s history. Their rise was supported by improved facilities and a structured long-term development approach.

Since reaching the top flight, Penybont has become a stable Cymru Premier side and has also achieved notable success in domestic cup competitions. The club reached the Welsh Cup final in 2021–22 and has regularly competed in the upper half of the league table. Their strong performances earned them qualification for European competition, where they represented Wales in the UEFA Europa Conference League qualifiers, marking an important milestone in the club’s short but rapidly developing history.

name: Afan Lido FC
content:
Afan Lido FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Port Talbot, Neath Port Talbot. The club was founded in 1967 following the opening of the Afan Lido Sports Centre, where it was originally created to provide organised football activity for local users. It gradually progressed through the Welsh football structure, moving from local leagues into the Welsh Football League and eventually becoming a regular participant in the national system. The team plays its home matches at the Marston’s Stadium (Lido Ground), which has a capacity of around 4,200 spectators.

Afan Lido became one of the founder members of the League of Wales in 1992 and quickly established itself as a competitive side in the early years of the national league. The club achieved notable success in cup competitions, winning the Welsh League Cup multiple times, and also finished near the top of the league in the mid-1990s, earning qualification for European competition. During this period, they represented Wales in the UEFA Cup, gaining experience against international opposition, although they were eliminated in the qualifying rounds.

In later years, the club experienced a mix of relegations, promotions, and rebuilding phases, reflecting a period of instability both on and off the pitch. Despite these challenges, Afan Lido has remained an established part of Welsh football and has continued to compete within the Cymru South and other tiers of the system. The club is also known for its strong local identity and rivalry with nearby Port Talbot Town, which has been a defining feature of its modern history.

name: Ton Pentre FC
content:
Ton Pentre FC is a Welsh football club based in the village of Ton Pentre in the Rhondda Valley. The current club was founded in 1935, although earlier versions of the team existed from the late 19th century. The club plays its home matches at Ynys Park and is known as the “Rhondda Bulldogs.” Over time, it became a well-known representative of football in the South Wales Valleys and developed within the Welsh football pyramid.

Historically, the club’s earlier incarnations achieved notable success in Welsh football, including reaching the Welsh Cup final in the 1921–22 season, where they finished as runners-up. In the post-war era, Ton Pentre competed strongly in regional Welsh leagues, winning divisional titles and establishing themselves as one of the competitive sides outside the top professional level. They also became involved in national restructuring of Welsh football and were part of the early development of the league system that eventually led to the modern national structure.

In the modern era, Ton Pentre have experienced both success and decline, moving between divisions within the Welsh football pyramid. They were founder members of the League of Wales in 1992 but later spent time outside the top tier after relegations and league restructuring. Despite fluctuations in performance, the club has remained active and continues to represent its local community, maintaining its identity as one of the traditional clubs from the Rhondda region.

name: Ebbw Vale FC
content:
Ebbw Vale FC was a Welsh football club based in Ebbw Vale, Blaenau Gwent, with origins dating back to 1888 and a reformation in 1907. The club played its home matches at Eugene Cross Park, a stadium with a capacity of around 8,000 spectators. Nicknamed “The Cowboys,” it became one of the established teams in South Wales football and competed in various regional and national competitions throughout its history.

The club was a founding member of the League of Wales in 1992 and spent its early years in the new national system. Ebbw Vale performed strongly in the mid-1990s, finishing 3rd in consecutive seasons and establishing themselves as one of the more competitive sides in the league. This success led to qualification for European competition, including participation in the UEFA Intertoto Cup, where they faced clubs from several European countries.

Despite on-field success, the club was expelled from the League of Wales before the 1998–99 season and subsequently went out of business in 1998. Their final competitive appearances came in European competition in the same period. After the club’s dissolution, attempts were later made to restore football in the town through phoenix clubs, continuing the football tradition in Ebbw Vale.

name: Neath FC
content:
Neath FC was a Welsh football club based in Neath, South Wales. The modern version of the club was formed in 2005 as Neath Athletic following a merger between Neath and Skewen Athletic. The team played its home matches at The Gnoll, a stadium with a capacity of around 6,000 spectators, and quickly progressed through the Welsh football system. In its early years, the club established itself as a strong side in the Welsh Football League before reaching the national top division.

After earning promotion to the Welsh Premier League, Neath became a competitive team at the highest level of Welsh football. The club achieved notable success in the early 2010s, finishing as high as third place in the league and competing for European qualification. During this period, Neath also strengthened its squad with several high-profile signings and became one of the more ambitious semi-professional clubs in Wales. This progress allowed them to take part in UEFA competition, where they represented Wales in European qualifiers.

Despite their sporting rise, Neath FC faced serious financial and licensing issues that ultimately led to the club’s downfall. In 2012, they were refused both domestic and UEFA licences for the following season, making them ineligible to continue in professional competition. Shortly afterwards, the club was wound up at the High Court, bringing an end to its short but eventful existence in Welsh football.

name: Carmarthen Town AFC
content:
Carmarthen Town AFC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Carmarthen, Carmarthenshire. The club was founded in 1948 and plays its home matches at Richmond Park, which has been its base since the early 1950s. Known by the nickname “The Old Gold,” the club’s identity is closely linked to its traditional gold and black colours. Over the years, Carmarthen Town has developed into a stable part of the Welsh football structure.

The club joined the Welsh Football League in the early 1950s and gradually progressed through the divisions before becoming part of the national top tier when the League of Wales was formed in 1992. Carmarthen Town spent many seasons in the Cymru Premier, where they achieved their strongest league finish of third place in the early 2000s. This success also helped them qualify for European competition, marking an important milestone in the club’s history.

In addition to league performance, Carmarthen Town has enjoyed success in domestic cup competitions, including winning the Welsh Cup and the Welsh League Cup. The club has also represented Wales in UEFA competitions on several occasions, facing international opponents in qualifying rounds. Although they were relegated from the top division in 2019–20, Carmarthen Town remains an established and competitive club within the Welsh football system.

name: Haverfordwest County AFC
content:
Haverfordwest County AFC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire. The club was founded in 1899 and has gone through several name changes, including Haverfordwest FC, Haverfordwest Town, and Haverfordwest Athletic, before adopting its current identity. It plays its home matches at Bridge Meadow Stadium and competes in the Cymru Premier, the top tier of Welsh football. The club is one of the established sides in West Wales football with a long history in the national league system.

Throughout its history, Haverfordwest County has experienced a mix of promotions, relegations, and restructuring within Welsh football. It was a long-standing member of the Welsh football pyramid and became part of the League of Wales when it was formed in 1992, although it briefly left the league in the mid-1990s before returning. The club has also achieved strong league performances, including a best finish of third place in the early 2000s, which marked one of its most successful periods. During this time, it also qualified for European competition.

In the modern era, Haverfordwest County has re-established itself as a stable Cymru Premier club. The team has returned to European qualification in recent seasons and continues to compete strongly in domestic competitions. Despite periods of relegation and rebuilding, the club has maintained its position in the Welsh football structure and remains an important representative of football in Pembrokeshire.

name: Aberystwyth Town FC
content:
Aberystwyth Town FC is a Welsh football club based in the coastal town of Aberystwyth, Ceredigion. The club was founded in 1884 and is one of the oldest football teams in Wales. It plays its home matches at Park Avenue, a stadium with a capacity of around 5,000 spectators, and is known by the nickname “The Seasiders” or “The Black and Greens.” The club has long been an important representative of Mid and West Wales football.

Throughout its history, Aberystwyth Town developed through early friendly matches and regional competitions before becoming more structured within the Welsh league system in the 20th century. The club achieved success in regional leagues and cup competitions and was one of the stronger sides in Mid-Wales football for many decades. In 1992, Aberystwyth became a founding member of the League of Wales (now Cymru Premier), and they immediately performed strongly, finishing near the top of the table in the early seasons.

In the modern era, Aberystwyth Town has remained a long-standing participant in the Welsh top division, although its league position has fluctuated over time. The club has also competed in European competitions such as the UEFA Intertoto Cup and UEFA Europa League qualifiers, facing clubs from across Europe. While not among the dominant teams in Wales, Aberystwyth Town is recognised for its stability, academy development, and long footballing tradition.

name: Conwy Borough FC
content:
Conwy Borough FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in the town of Conwy, North Wales. The club was originally formed in 1977 as Conwy United through the merger of Conwy Town and Conwy Royal British Legion, aiming to create a stronger local team. It later became known as Conwy Borough FC in 2012. The club plays its home matches at Y Morfa Stadium and has long been a key representative of football in the Conwy area.

Throughout its history, the club progressed through the Welsh league system, achieving success in regional competitions and establishing itself in higher divisions. Conwy United enjoyed notable success in the 1980s and 1990s, including league titles and strong performances in national competitions. In the mid-1990s, the club reached one of its peak periods, finishing highly in the League of Wales and even qualifying for European competition in the UEFA Intertoto Cup, where it faced clubs from across Europe.

In later years, the club experienced financial difficulties and fluctuations in performance, leading to relegations and rebuilding phases. Despite this, Conwy Borough continued to compete within the Welsh football pyramid, moving between divisions and maintaining its presence in North Welsh football. More recently, the club has undergone further restructuring and changes, including mergers aimed at strengthening its long-term stability and development within the local football community.

name: Llandudno FC
content:
Llandudno FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in the seaside town of Llandudno, Conwy County Borough. The club was originally formed in 1988, although football in the town dates back to the late 19th century through earlier sides such as Gloddaeth Rovers and Llandudno Swifts. It plays its home matches at Maesdu Park and is commonly known as “The Seasiders.” The club has developed into one of the established teams in North Welsh football.

Throughout its history, Llandudno progressed through the Welsh football pyramid, competing in regional leagues before rising to national-level football. The club achieved significant success in the 2014–15 season when it won the Cymru Alliance, earning promotion to the Welsh Premier League for the first time. This marked a major milestone, as the club entered the top tier of Welsh football and began competing against the strongest teams in the country.

In its first spell in the Cymru Premier, Llandudno achieved notable success by finishing third in the 2015–16 season, which qualified them for the UEFA Europa League qualifiers. However, the club was later relegated in the 2018–19 season and returned to the second tier, the Cymru North. More recently, the club has continued to compete at a high level within the Welsh system and has maintained ambitions to return to the top division.

name: Port Talbot Town FC
content:
Port Talbot Town Football Club is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Port Talbot, Wales. It was originally founded in 1901 as Port Talbot Athletic and later became the modern club after developments following the Second World War. The team is commonly known as “The Steelmen” and plays its home matches at Victoria Road.

For much of its early history, the club competed in lower regional leagues in Wales before gradually progressing through the Welsh football pyramid. In 2000, Port Talbot Town earned promotion to the League of Wales (later the Welsh Premier League), and in 2001 it adopted its current name. Over the following years, the club established itself in the top tier of Welsh football, often competing in mid-table positions and occasionally challenging for higher finishes.

One of the club’s most successful periods came in the late 2000s and early 2010s, when it achieved strong league finishes, including a third-place result in the 2009–10 season. This performance qualified Port Talbot Town for its first participation in European competition, entering the UEFA Europa League in the 2010–11 season. Despite these achievements, the club has also faced financial and administrative challenges, including relegations and restructuring in later years, but it has continued to remain an active part of Welsh football.

name: Wrexham AFC
content:
Wrexham AFC is a Welsh professional football club based in Wrexham, Wales. Founded in 1864, it is the oldest football club in Wales and one of the oldest professional football clubs in the world. The team is traditionally known as “The Red Dragons” and plays its home matches at the Racecourse Ground, which is widely recognised as the oldest international football stadium still in use. The club currently competes in the English football league system, despite being based in Wales.

Throughout its long history, Wrexham spent many years competing in the lower divisions of the English Football League after joining in the early 20th century. The club remained in the Football League for decades before being relegated to non-league football in 2008. During its time outside the league, Wrexham experienced a difficult period but also became known for its strong supporter base and resilience, regularly pushing for promotion back into the professional tiers.

In recent years, the club has gained significant international attention following its takeover in 2020 by actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney. This new ownership brought increased investment, global media coverage, and a surge in popularity, especially through the documentary series about the club. Under their leadership, Wrexham achieved remarkable sporting success, including multiple consecutive promotions, rapidly climbing through the English football pyramid and returning to higher divisions after years outside the top tiers.

name: Cefn Druids AFC
content:
Cefn Druids AFC is a Welsh football club based in Rhosymedre, Wrexham County Borough. The club traces its origins back to 1872, making it one of the oldest football clubs in Wales. It was originally founded by Llewelyn Kenrick and later developed through a series of mergers, most notably becoming Cefn Druids in 1992 after the unification of Druids United and Cefn Albion. The team is known as “The Ancients” and traditionally plays in black and white striped kits, hosting home matches at The Rock stadium.

Historically, the club has played an important role in early Welsh football, with its predecessor Druids FC achieving significant success in the late 19th century. Druids were one of the founding clubs in Welsh football competitions and became one of the most successful early sides in the Welsh Cup, winning it multiple times. Cefn Druids as a modern entity continued this legacy by progressing through the Welsh football pyramid and establishing itself in national competitions.

In more recent decades, Cefn Druids has moved between the top tiers of Welsh football, including the Cymru Premier and Cymru North. The club reached notable milestones such as competing in the Welsh Cup final in the 2011–12 season and qualifying for European competition in the UEFA Europa League. Despite financial difficulties and periods of instability, including relegations and a temporary withdrawal from competition, the club has remained an important part of Welsh football culture and has continued to rebuild and participate in domestic leagues.

name: Shrewsbury Town FC
content:
Shrewsbury Town Football Club is a professional football club based in Shrewsbury, Shropshire, England. Founded in 1886, the club has spent most of its history competing in the lower divisions of English football. It became a member of the Football League in 1950 and has since played across the third and fourth tiers, with occasional relegations outside the league system in its history.

Throughout its development, Shrewsbury Town has moved between different stadiums, most notably playing at Gay Meadow for nearly a century before relocating to New Meadow in 2007. The club has experienced several promotions and relegations over the decades, including winning lower division titles and establishing itself as a regular Football League side. It has also taken part in cup competitions such as the Welsh Cup, where it achieved notable success for an English club.

In modern times, Shrewsbury Town has generally competed in League One and League Two of the English football pyramid. The club is known for its resilience and ability to stabilize after relegations, often rebuilding its squad and returning to higher divisions. Despite fluctuating performances, it remains a well-established professional side with a long-standing presence in English football.

name: Chirk AAA FC
content:
Chirk Amateur Athletic Association Football Club is a Welsh football club based in Chirk, Wrexham County Borough. Founded in 1876, it is one of the oldest football clubs in Wales and was among the founding members of the Football Association of Wales. The club is nicknamed “The Colliers,” reflecting the area’s industrial and mining heritage, and it plays its home matches at Holyhead Road stadium.

During the late 19th century, Chirk became one of the strongest teams in Welsh football, achieving major success in national competitions. The club won the Welsh Cup multiple times during this period and also played a key role in the early development of organised football in Wales. Several notable players from this era went on to represent Wales or achieve success in English football, helping to build the club’s historic reputation.

In modern times, Chirk AAA has mainly competed in the lower tiers of the Welsh football league system, frequently moving between regional divisions. The club has experienced periods of success, including league titles and cup victories at semi-professional level, but has also faced challenges with relegations and rebuilding phases. Despite this, it remains an important historic club within Welsh football with a strong local identity and long-standing tradition.

name: Merthyr Tydfil FC
content:
Merthyr Tydfil Football Club was a Welsh football club based in Merthyr Tydfil, South Wales. It was formed in 1945 following the closure of the town’s previous senior club and played its home matches at Penydarren Park. The team was known as “The Martyrs” and competed mainly in the English non-league system, where it built a strong reputation in regional football competitions.

In its early years, the club enjoyed significant success, particularly in the Southern League, where it won multiple championships during the late 1940s and early 1950s. Despite its strong performances on the pitch and success in competitions such as the Welsh Cup, the club was never elected to the English Football League. Over time, Merthyr Tydfil became a well-established non-league side, experiencing periods of both success and decline across several decades.

One of the club’s most notable achievements came in the late 1980s, when it won the Welsh Cup and earned a place in European competition, where it famously defeated Italian side Atalanta at home in the Cup Winners’ Cup. However, financial difficulties eventually led to the club’s liquidation in 2010. It was then reformed as Merthyr Town, which continues the footballing tradition in the town within the English football pyramid.

name: Telford United FC
content:
Telford United Football Club was an English football club based in Telford, Shropshire. The club was originally formed in 1872 and spent most of its history competing in the lower tiers of English football and non-league competitions. Over time, it became well known for its strong performances in cup competitions, particularly the FA Trophy and FA Cup, while also being a long-standing member of non-league football in England.

During its existence, Telford United achieved notable success in national competitions, especially the FA Trophy, which it won multiple times, and it also became known as a “giant-killer” in the FA Cup for defeating higher-league opposition. The club was one of the founder members of the Alliance Premier League in 1979 and remained a competitive side at that level for many years, often finishing in respectable mid-table positions and occasionally pushing for higher achievements.

Despite its sporting achievements, the club faced financial difficulties in the early 2000s. In the 2003–04 season it competed in the Conference Premier but ultimately collapsed in 2004 due to financial problems. Following its dissolution, supporters quickly formed a successor club, AFC Telford United, which continued the football tradition in the town and took over as the modern representative team.

name: Oswestry United FC
content:
Oswestry United Football Club was a Welsh football club based in Oswestry, Shropshire. It was formed in September 1893 following the collapse of the earlier Oswestry FC The club played its home matches at Victoria Road and competed in regional competitions such as the Shropshire & District League, later also taking part in the Combination and other cross-border leagues. It became an established team in the early development of football in the Welsh and English border regions.

During its existence, Oswestry United achieved notable success in both league and cup competitions. The club won the Welsh Cup twice, in 1901 and 1907, and also secured victories in the Shropshire Senior Cup. These achievements made it one of the stronger regional sides of its era, capable of competing against well-established Welsh clubs. One of its most famous successes was its 1901 Welsh Cup win, which attracted significant local support and attention.

The club’s decline began during the First World War, when many players left due to military service, making it difficult to continue competing. By 1914–15, Oswestry United was unable to fulfil fixtures and was eventually removed from competition. After the war, the club did not reform, and it was effectively replaced in the town’s football structure by a new club formed in 1920.

name: Crewe Alexandra FC
content:
Crewe Alexandra Football Club is a professional football club based in Crewe, Cheshire, England. Founded in 1877 as part of the Crewe Alexandra Cricket Club, it was named after Princess Alexandra. The club played its first matches in the late 19th century and gradually became established in English football, developing a long-standing identity linked to the town’s railway heritage and earning the nickname “The Railwaymen.”

In its early history, Crewe Alexandra competed in the Football League and experienced a mix of early success and setbacks, including reaching the FA Cup semi-finals in 1888 and later losing its league status in the 1890s before rejoining the system. Over time, the club became known for fluctuating between divisions in the lower tiers of English football, with periods in the third and fourth levels of the league structure. Despite this, it built a reputation for resilience and steady rebuilding.

In the modern era, Crewe Alexandra is widely recognised for its strong emphasis on youth development, producing several notable players who went on to represent England and other national teams. The club has achieved promotions between League Two and League One, as well as success in domestic competitions such as the Football League Trophy. Under long-term managerial stability, particularly during the tenure of Dario Gradi, Crewe became known for developing technical, possession-based football and maintaining a respected academy system.

name: Hereford United FC
content:
Hereford United Football Club was an English association football club based in Hereford, Herefordshire. It was founded in 1924 and played its home matches throughout its existence at Edgar Street. The club competed for many years in the lower divisions of English football, mainly moving between the Football League’s lower tiers and non-league competitions. It was known by the nickname “The Bulls” and became closely associated with its passionate local support and long-standing rivalries, particularly with nearby clubs.

One of the most famous moments in the club’s history came in 1972, when Hereford achieved a major FA Cup shock by defeating top-flight Newcastle United in a replay. This run brought national attention to the club and was followed by election into the Football League, where Hereford quickly rose through the divisions, even winning the Third Division title in 1975–76. However, after reaching the second tier, the club struggled to maintain its position and eventually settled back into the lower divisions for much of its later Football League history.

In its final decades, Hereford United experienced both sporting challenges and financial instability. The club spent long periods in non-league football, including repeated promotion pushes and play-off attempts, but also faced mounting financial difficulties. These problems ultimately led to severe sanctions and expulsion from competitions, and in December 2014 the club was wound up in the High Court, ending its existence after 90 years. A new phoenix club was later formed to continue football in the city.

name: Connah's Quay & Shotton FC
content:
Connah’s Quay & Shotton FC was a Welsh football club based in Connah’s Quay, Flintshire. The club originated in 1905 as Connah’s Quay Twenties after the collapse of an earlier local team, and it quickly established itself in regional competitions such as the Chester & District League and The Combination. It went through several early reorganisations and mergers with local sides, including Hawarden Bridge, which helped shape its identity in North Wales football.

During the 1910s and 1920s, the club competed in a range of regional leagues, including the North Wales Alliance, the Cheshire County League, and later the Welsh National League (North). It became a semi-professional side and was among the stronger teams in the region, even applying unsuccessfully for election to the Football League in 1929. The club also participated in the FA Cup and experienced a relatively competitive period, including finishing near the top of the Cheshire County League in its later years.

Despite these moments of success, Connah’s Quay & Shotton struggled financially and competitively in its final years. After fluctuating league performances and growing financial pressure, the club ultimately resigned from the Cheshire County League during the 1931–32 season and was dissolved in November 1931. Its collapse marked the end of one of the early prominent football teams in the Connah’s Quay area, though later clubs continued the town’s football tradition.

name: Newport County AFC
content:
Newport County AFC is a professional football club based in Newport, South Wales. It was founded in 1912 and originally played in the Southern League before becoming a founding member of the Football League Third Division in 1920. The club is commonly known as “The Exiles” and plays its home matches at Rodney Parade, sharing the stadium with other sports teams. Over its history, Newport County has been closely associated with the lower tiers of English football while maintaining a strong local identity in Welsh football culture.

In its early Football League years, the club experienced mixed success, including promotion and relegation between divisions. One of its most successful early achievements came in the 1938–39 season when it won the Third Division South title. After World War II, the club briefly competed in the Second Division but struggled to maintain that level and was eventually relegated again, spending much of the following decades in the lower divisions.

The club later faced financial difficulties in the 1980s, which led to relegations and ultimately its collapse in 1989. It was then reformed and restarted in non-league football, gradually rebuilding through the Welsh and English league systems. Over time, Newport County returned to the Football League in 2013 after winning the Conference Premier play-off final, marking a major revival in its modern history and re-establishing itself as a professional league club.

name: Flint Town United FC
content:
Flint Town United Football Club is a Welsh football club based in Flint, Flintshire, and is one of the older teams in North Wales, with origins dating back to 1886 when it was originally founded as Flint FC The early club played at Strand Park and quickly became part of the regional football scene, competing in competitions such as the Welsh Amateur Cup, where it reached the first final in 1890–91. Over time, the club developed through mergers and reorganisations, eventually forming Flint Town United after combining with Flint Athletic following the Second World War.

In the early decades of its existence, the club experienced periods of strong regional success. It won the North Wales Coast League in the 1890s and later achieved success in various regional leagues and cup competitions. One of its most notable early achievements came in 1954, when Flint won the Welsh Cup, defeating Chester City in the final after a strong cup run that included victories over several established Welsh sides. This period is often seen as one of the club’s historical peaks in competitive football.

In the modern era, Flint Town United has mainly competed within the Welsh football league system, moving between divisions such as the Cymru Alliance, Cymru North, and Cymru Premier. The club has experienced promotions, relegations, and league restructuring, but has remained a consistent presence in Welsh semi-professional football. Despite fluctuations in performance, it continues to represent the town of Flint at the national level and maintains its identity as a long-standing community-focused club.

name: White Stars FC
content:
White Stars FC was an early association football club from Newtown, Powys in Wales, active in the late 19th century. The club was founded in 1875 and is also known as Newtown White Stars. It is considered one of the early football teams in the region and is linked historically to the development of modern football in Newtown. The club played its home matches on Welshpool Road and used the white star emblem as its identifying symbol.

In its early years, White Stars FC competed in local and regional football, taking part in competitions such as early Welsh Cup ties and friendly matches against other Welsh and border clubs. The team was part of the rapidly growing football scene in Wales during the 1870s and 1880s, a period when organised competition was still developing. Some players associated with the club were notable enough to receive recognition at higher levels, including international appearances.

The club was short-lived, as it struggled to maintain long-term stability in the competitive environment of early Welsh football. By the early 1880s, White Stars FC had effectively ceased to exist, and its place in the local football structure was absorbed by other emerging clubs in Newtown. Despite its brief existence, it remains part of the early football history of Wales and contributed to the formation of later clubs in the area.

name: Oswestry FC
content:
Oswestry FC was an early association football club based in Oswestry, Shropshire. It was founded in September 1875 as an offshoot of the local cricket club and is considered one of the earliest organised football teams in the town. The club played its home matches at the Oswestry Cricket Ground and wore blue kits, establishing itself as one of the pioneering sides in the development of football in the Welsh-English border region.

During its early years, Oswestry became one of the stronger regional teams and competed in some of the first organised cup competitions in Wales and the border counties. It took part in the inaugural Welsh Cup in the late 1870s and was also involved in early Shropshire and regional competitions. The club reached the semi-finals of early cup tournaments and was notable for contributing several players to representative matches, including early Welsh international fixtures. It also had periods of absorbing or combining with local sides, which helped strengthen its squad in key seasons.

Oswestry FC achieved one of its greatest successes in the early 1880s when it became the first English club to win the Welsh Cup, defeating Druids in the final. The club also had notable runs in the FA Cup, including reaching the later stages against stronger opposition from larger English and Scottish sides. However, by the late 1880s and early 1890s, the club began to decline and eventually disbanded around 1891, later being succeeded by new Oswestry-based clubs that continued the town’s football tradition.

name: Lovell's Athletic FC
content:
Lovell’s Athletic FC was a Welsh works football club based in Newport, Monmouthshire, formed in 1918 as the team of the Lovell’s sweet factory. The club played its home matches at Rexville on Alder Street and was commonly known as “the Toffeemen.” It competed in a variety of Welsh, English, and regional leagues during its existence, becoming a strong semi-professional side in South Wales football.

During the 1920s and 1930s, the club established itself as one of the leading teams in regional competitions, winning the Western Football League in its debut season and later claiming additional league titles. It also competed in the Southern League and Welsh Football League, enjoying a particularly successful period in the late 1930s and after World War II. One of its standout achievements was winning the Welsh Cup in 1948, along with a notable FA Cup run that included reaching the third round in the 1945–46 season.

In the post-war years, Lovell’s Athletic continued to be a strong force in Welsh football, winning multiple league and cup honours and even outperforming local rivals during periods when other Newport teams were inactive. However, by the late 1950s and 1960s, declining attendance and financial pressures made it difficult to sustain semi-professional football. The club eventually left higher-level competition and was dissolved in 1969, bringing an end to over 50 years of football history.

name: Caernarfon Town FC
content:
Caernarfon Town FC is a Welsh football club based in Caernarfon, Gwynedd, founded in 1937 by local supporters following a long tradition of earlier clubs in the town. The team is known as “The Canaries” because of its yellow and green kit, a nickname that dates back to the late 19th century. It plays its home matches at The Oval, a historic ground that has hosted football in Caernarfon since the 1880s.

The club developed through the Welsh football pyramid, competing successfully in regional leagues such as the Welsh League (North) before moving into stronger cross-border competitions in England, including the Lancashire Combination and later the North West Counties League. During the 1980s, Caernarfon Town achieved one of its strongest periods, including winning league titles and reaching the FA Cup third round, where they famously faced higher-division opposition.

In 1995, the club joined the League of Wales (now Cymru Premier), where it has since competed at the top level of Welsh football, experiencing both promotions and relegations. In recent years, Caernarfon Town has enjoyed renewed success, including cup victories and qualification for European competitions, marking one of the most successful modern eras in its history.

name: South Liverpool FC
content:
South Liverpool FC was a football club based in Liverpool, England, originally formed in 1897 under the name African Royal before later becoming South Liverpool. The club played in regional competitions such as The Combination and the Lancashire Combination, establishing itself as a competitive non-league side in the early 20th century. In 1921, the original club effectively ceased after relocating and merging into what became New Brighton AFC, which continued its Football League journey.

A new South Liverpool FC was founded in 1935 and entered the Lancashire Combination, quickly finding success in regional football. The club became one of the stronger non-league sides in northern England, winning league titles and cup competitions before the Second World War. One of its most notable achievements was winning the Welsh Cup in 1939, and it also built a reputation for producing talented players and competing strongly in FA Cup ties against higher-level opposition.

In the post-war era, South Liverpool continued competing mainly in the Cheshire League, Lancashire Combination, and later the Northern Premier League. The club experienced periods of success in cup competitions, but gradually declined due to financial pressures and stadium issues. Its historic ground, Holly Park, was eventually lost, and the club ceased first-team operations in 1991, with formal liquidation following shortly after. A successor club was later formed to continue its football tradition at a lower level.

name: Borough United FC
content:
Borough United FC was a Welsh football club based in Llandudno Junction, formed in 1954 through the merger of Llandudno Junction and Conwy Borough. The club was created to combine two struggling local sides and quickly established itself in Welsh regional football. It played its home matches at Nant-y-Coed and competed mainly in the Welsh National League (North), becoming a strong semi-professional team in North Wales.

During its short existence, Borough United enjoyed a surprisingly successful period in the early 1960s. The club won the Welsh National League (North) twice and achieved its greatest triumph in 1962–63 by winning the Welsh Cup, defeating Newport County in the final. This success made them one of the most remarkable underdog stories in Welsh football at the time and earned them a place in European competition.

In the 1963–64 season, Borough United competed in the UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup, where they achieved a historic win by defeating Sliema Wanderers of Malta before being eliminated by Slovan Bratislava. Despite these achievements, the club struggled with financial and infrastructure issues. After losing access to their ground and failing to secure a suitable alternative, Borough United left league football and dissolved in 1967, bringing an end to a brief but notable chapter in Welsh football history.

name: Prestatyn Town FC
content:
Prestatyn Town FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in Prestatyn, Denbighshire. The club was founded in 1910 and is nicknamed “The Seasiders” due to its coastal location near the Irish Sea. It plays its home matches at Bastion Road, which has been the club’s long-term ground after earlier football activity in the town dating back to the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Throughout its history, Prestatyn Town competed mainly in regional Welsh leagues before progressing through the Welsh football pyramid. The club spent time in competitions such as the Clwyd League and Welsh Alliance League, gradually building success at semi-professional level. A major breakthrough came in the late 2000s when they earned promotion to the Welsh Premier League after winning the Cymru Alliance in the 2007–08 season, marking their rise to the top tier of Welsh football.

The club’s most successful modern period came in the early 2010s. In the 2012–13 season, Prestatyn Town achieved historic success by winning the Welsh Cup, which allowed them to compete in European competition for the first time. They also played in the UEFA Europa League, marking a major milestone in the club’s history. After this peak, the club experienced relegation and rebuilding phases, but it has remained an established presence in the Welsh football system.

name: Aberdare Athletic FC
content:
Aberdare Athletic FC was a Welsh football club based in Aberdare, Glamorgan. The club was founded in 1893 and played its home matches at the Athletic Ground. It became part of the early development of organised football in Wales and competed in regional competitions before progressing to higher levels of English football structure.

The club achieved a major step forward in 1921 when it joined the Football League Third Division South. In its early league years, Aberdare showed competitive performances and even managed respectable mid-table finishes. However, the club struggled with financial instability and declining results during the mid-1920s, which made it difficult to maintain its Football League status.

In 1927, Aberdare Athletic finished at the bottom of the Third Division South and failed re-election to the Football League, being replaced by Torquay United. After losing its league place, the club was unable to sustain itself at the same level and was dissolved in 1928. Its history remains part of the early story of Welsh clubs competing within the English football system.

name: Pontypridd AFC
content:
Pontypridd AFC was a Welsh professional football club based in Pontypridd, Glamorgan. It was founded in 1911 with the aim of establishing senior-level association football in the town and played its home matches at Taff Vale Park in Treforest. The club is often associated with the nickname “The Dragons” and was part of the early development of organised football in South Wales.

During its competitive years, Pontypridd AFC played in the Southern League from its formation and remained active until 1926. The club also competed in the Welsh League, where it achieved success by winning the championship in the 1923–24 season. In cup competitions, it reached the Welsh Cup final on multiple occasions, including in 1912, 1913, and 1921, and also won the South Wales FA Senior Cup in 1925.

Despite these achievements, the club eventually struggled to sustain itself at a professional level and ceased operations in 1926. Its closure marked the end of one of the early professional football projects in Pontypridd, although the town later saw new football clubs emerge to continue its sporting tradition. The legacy of Pontypridd AFC remains part of the early football history of South Wales and its participation in cross-border English and Welsh competitions.

name: Westminster Rovers FC
content:
Westminster Rovers FC was a Welsh football club based in Wrexham, Wales. It was formed around 1889 as the team of the Westminster Colliery and played its home matches at Stansty Park. The club wore white kits and quickly became involved in the developing football scene in North Wales during the late 19th century. It is considered part of the early wave of organised works teams that formed around local industries.

During its competitive years, Westminster Rovers were one of the stronger regional sides. They competed in the Welsh Senior League, where they achieved notable success, including winning the league title in 1893–94 and finishing as runners-up in other seasons. The club also enjoyed strong Welsh Cup runs, reaching the final twice in the early 1890s but losing on both occasions to Chirk.

Despite these achievements, the club’s existence was relatively short-lived. Westminster Rovers were last recorded in competition in 1897, after which they disappeared from senior football. Although brief, their history reflects the early development of football in Wales, where many industrial and works-based clubs played an important role before later professional structures became established.

name: Ruthin Town FC
content:
Ruthin Town FC is a Welsh semi-professional football club based in the town of Ruthin, Denbighshire. The club is generally traced back to the late 19th century, with early football activity in the town recorded around 1870, although the modern club structure was re-established in the mid-20th century. Ruthin plays its home matches at the Memorial Playing Fields and is known by the nickname “The Town.” It is part of the long football tradition in the Vale of Clwyd area.

Throughout its history, Ruthin Town has competed mainly in regional Welsh leagues before progressing into higher tiers of the Welsh football pyramid. The club has spent many seasons in competitions such as the Welsh National League (Wrexham Area) and later the Cymru Alliance (now Cymru North). Over time, it became a stable semi-professional side, regularly finishing in competitive positions and also achieving cup successes in regional competitions.

In the modern era, Ruthin Town continues to compete in the Cymru North, the second tier of Welsh football. The club is known for its long-standing youth development system and steady presence in Welsh semi-professional football. It has experienced promotions, relegations, and rebuilding phases but remains an established community club with a strong local identity and a long footballing tradition in North Wales.

name: Aberdare Town FC
content:
Aberdare Town FC is a Welsh football club based in Aberdare, Rhondda Cynon Taf. The club was originally founded in 1892 as Aberaman Athletic, and its early history is closely tied to several mergers and reorganisations involving nearby teams, including Aberdare Athletic. These changes reflected the shifting structure of football in the region during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The modern identity of Aberdare Town was eventually established in the mid-20th century after a series of re-formations and splits between local clubs.

Throughout its history, the club has mainly competed in the Welsh football league system, playing in various regional divisions and gradually becoming a stable semi-professional side. After earlier club versions in the town were involved in the Football League era during the 1920s, Aberdare’s football structure continued at a lower level following those teams’ decline. Over time, Aberdare Town built its presence in Welsh domestic competitions, focusing on local league football and player development rather than national league participation.

In more recent years, Aberdare Town FC has continued to operate as a community-based club, participating in South Wales regional leagues. It has experienced relegations and restructuring within the Welsh football pyramid but remains active with senior and youth teams. The club’s modern identity reflects the long football tradition in Aberdare, maintaining continuity with earlier historic clubs from the town while competing at a semi-professional level today.

name: Whitchurch FC
content:
Whitchurch Football Club was an English association football club based in Whitchurch, Shropshire. Founded in October 1871, it was one of the early football teams in the region and played an important role in the development of organised football in the Welsh–English border area. The club competed in various early regional competitions and also took part in the Welsh Cup despite being based in England.

During its competitive history, Whitchurch became a strong side in early league football, particularly in The Combination, where it won the league title on multiple occasions. The club also achieved notable success in the Welsh Cup, reaching the final twice in the early 20th century (1906 and 1907), finishing as runner-up on both occasions. These results established Whitchurch as one of the stronger non-league teams in its region during that period.

However, the club eventually declined in the 20th century as football structures evolved and stronger professional sides emerged. Whitchurch FC ceased operations in 1985 after more than a century of activity. Its history remains part of the early cross-border football tradition between England and Wales, and its legacy is often remembered alongside other historic Whitchurch-based clubs.

name: Northwich Victoria FC
content:
Northwich Victoria Football Club is an English association football club based in Northwich, Cheshire. Founded in 1874, it is one of the oldest clubs in English football and has a long history of competing in both league and non-league systems. The club originally played at the Drill Field, its historic home for over a century, before later moving to Victoria Stadium in Wincham, and has since experienced several ground-sharing arrangements due to financial and infrastructural difficulties.

In its early history, Northwich Victoria was one of the prominent sides in northern English football, becoming a founder member of the Football League Second Division in 1892, although it only remained in the league for two seasons. Over the decades, the club became a strong non-league presence, competing in competitions such as the Cheshire League, the Northern Premier League, and later the National League system. It also earned recognition for FA Cup runs and FA Trophy success, establishing a reputation as a resilient and competitive non-league side.

In modern times, Northwich Victoria has faced significant financial and organisational challenges, including loss of its stadium, relegations, and repeated restructuring. Despite this instability, the club has continued to operate within the English football pyramid, often sharing grounds and rebuilding its squad and management structure. Its history is marked by persistence through hardship, with strong community support helping the club maintain its identity over more than a century of football tradition.

name: Kidderminster Harriers FC
content:
Kidderminster Harriers FC is a professional football club based in Kidderminster, Worcestershire, England. Founded in 1886, the club is one of the most established non-league sides in English football history and is currently competing in the National League North. They are known by the nicknames “The Harriers” and “The Carpetmen” and have played their entire history at Aggborough Stadium, which has been their home since the late 19th century.

Throughout their history, Kidderminster Harriers have been a strong presence in non-league football, particularly in regional competitions and national cups. They were founder members of early regional leagues and later became champions of several divisions, including multiple league titles in the Birmingham and District/West Midlands leagues. The club also achieved major success in cup competitions, most notably winning the FA Trophy in 1987 and building a reputation as one of the strongest non-league sides in England.

In modern times, the club has experienced both promotion to and relegation from the English Football League. A major highlight came in 1999–2000 when they won the Football Conference and earned promotion to the Football League for the first time in their history. They spent five seasons in League Two before being relegated in 2005, and since then have moved between the National League and National League North, continuing to compete at the top levels of non-league football.

name: Davenham FC
content:
Davenham FC was an English association football club based in Davenham, Cheshire. It was founded in 1879 and played its home matches at the Oddfellows Arms ground. The club was nicknamed “the Villagers” and was part of the early development of organised football in the Cheshire region during the late 19th century.

During its competitive years, Davenham FC became one of the stronger amateur sides in the area. The club achieved its most successful period in the mid-1880s, particularly in the 1885–86 season when it won the Cheshire Senior Cup and had a strong run in the FA Cup. That campaign included notable victories against established regional teams and helped establish Davenham as a competitive side in both Cheshire and Welsh cup competitions.

The club also reached one of its greatest achievements in the Welsh Cup, where it advanced to the final in the 1886–87 season, ultimately finishing as runners-up. However, as football became more professionalised, Davenham struggled to compete at the same level. In 1889, it merged with Hartford St John’s and later became part of an amalgamation involving Northwich Victoria, effectively ending the club’s independent existence around 1890.

name: Merthyr Town FC
content:
Merthyr Town FC is a Welsh football club based in Merthyr Tydfil, South Wales. The modern club was formed in 2010 following the liquidation of Merthyr Tydfil FC, continuing the football tradition at Penydarren Park. It is a fan-owned, community-focused team and currently competes in the English football league system, representing the town in cross-border competition rather than the Welsh domestic pyramid.

The club’s history is closely linked to the highly successful Merthyr Tydfil A.FC, founded in 1945, which became one of the strongest non-league sides in Britain during the late 1940s and early 1950s. That earlier club won multiple Southern League titles and Welsh Cups, and even competed in European competition after winning the Welsh Cup in 1987. Despite on-field success, financial instability prevented long-term stability at higher levels.

Since its reformation as Merthyr Town, the club has worked its way back up through the non-league system, achieving promotions from the Western League and Southern League divisions. It has experienced both strong league campaigns and rebuilding periods, while maintaining solid community support and regular attendance at Penydarren Park. Today, it continues to compete in the National League North, aiming to progress further up the English football pyramid.

name: Stourbridge FC
content:
Stourbridge Football Club is an English association football club based in Stourbridge, West Midlands. Founded in 1876 as Stourbridge Standard, the club is nicknamed “The Glassboys” due to the town’s historic glassmaking industry. It plays its home matches at the War Memorial Athletic Ground in Amblecote, a long-standing venue that has hosted football in the town since the late 19th century.

In its early history, Stourbridge competed in regional competitions such as the Birmingham & District League, where it established itself as a competitive amateur side. The club experienced several strong periods, including winning league titles and multiple regional cup competitions, particularly in the 1920s and post-Second World War era. It also built a reputation for producing notable cup runs and developing players who later moved to higher-level English clubs.

In the modern era, Stourbridge has been a consistent non-league side within the English football pyramid, competing mainly in the Southern League and other regional divisions. The club has achieved notable FA Cup runs, including reaching the later qualifying rounds and even the third round in the 2016–17 season, marking one of its most successful modern campaigns. Despite fluctuations between divisions, it remains a stable semi-professional club with a strong local identity and regular community support.

name: Hednesford Town FC
content:
Hednesford Town FC is an English football club based in Hednesford, Staffordshire. The club was formed in 1880 through the merger of two local teams, the Red & Whites and Hill Top, and spent its early decades playing in regional and local leagues. They are known as “The Pitmen” due to the area’s coal mining heritage and play their home matches at Keys Park stadium.

During the late 20th century, Hednesford Town rose through the non-league system, joining higher-level regional competitions and eventually reaching the Football Conference in the mid-1990s. One of the club’s most successful periods came in this era, when they achieved strong league finishes and notable FA Cup runs, including victories over higher-division opposition. They also reached the fourth round of the FA Cup in the 1996–97 season, one of the most famous highlights in their history.

In cup competitions, the club achieved its greatest success by winning the FA Trophy in the 2003–04 season, defeating Canvey Island in the final. In the following years, Hednesford experienced promotions and relegations across the National League and regional divisions, reflecting a fluctuating but competitive history in English non-league football. Despite setbacks, the club has remained a strong presence in Staffordshire football with a loyal supporter base.
